newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Mandela talks negotiation to Irish foes.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mandela talks negotiation to Irish foes.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela on Saturday met visiting delegations from Northern Ireland's divided political factions at a seaside resort east of Cape Town, the South African government said.
"He (Mandela) spent about one hour sharing his thoughts about negotiation and the challenges the process poses for political leaders," the government said in a brief statement.

No further details were released of the meeting, underway near Arniston village in a high-security complex used under apartheid for the development of a missile engine and since then mainly for conferences and sensitive negotiations.
South Africa has said the meeting is not an attempt at mediation but merely a forum to pass on experiences of its own dramatic shift from white rule to democracy.
Both Sinn Fein and the Ulster Unionists sent delegations to the talks, but a South African minister said on Friday arrangements were in place to ensure they did not have to meet or see each other.

The other Irish participants represent the Alliance Party, the Social Democratic Labour Party, Democratic Unionist Party, the Ulster Democratic Party, Labour Party, Progressive Unionist Party and the Women's Coalition.
